correctness.rationale: For every trajectory the positive opinion floor and four explicit length-four local paths imply a_i^k(t+4)>=eta b_i(t). Irreducibility propagates one positive initial b through at most n-1 directed edges; monotonic b gives b_i(t)>=B at time 6(n-1). Consequently a_i^k(t)>=eta B and row-stochastic physical contacts yield s_i(t+1)<=(1-rho)s_i(t) for all t>=T. The proof accounts for m=2, n=1, zero initial opinions, arbitrary admissible feedback, and initial dissatisfied-only seeds. Exact rational matrix checks and independent coupled-model simulation support arithmetic without claiming infinite certification.

value.rationale: The result determines universal global depletion and persistence under strong feedback even when the source allows multiple positive equilibria, distinguishing persistence from full-state convergence. It gives a motivated structural test for competitive adoption dynamics and rates valid across all finite connected network topologies, not an arbitrary numerical case or routine parameter increment.
